title: Yalta this is not: The Xi–Trump–Putin meeting is China’s show and America’s loss
gist: Chatham House argues the Shenzhen Xi–Trump–Putin summit is Chinese showmanship, not a new Yalta: China holds the leverage (critical minerals, Nvidia chips), Putin gains legitimacy despite a war-drained economy, Trump loses US moral standing, and Ukraine and Europe are left exposed — pushing Europe and smaller states to build their own common front.

insights.claim: Chatham House argues the Xi–Trump–Putin summit in Shenzhen is showmanship rather than a Yalta-style carve-up, and any deals will be small and in China's favour unless Trump sides with Russia over Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Discount headline-grabbing 'grand bargain' narratives from the summit; expect marginal outcomes skewed toward Beijing.
insights.quote: Any deals to be done are small – and they are all in China’s favour, unless Trump decides to side with Russia over Ukraine.
insights.locator: But this week’s meeting is no Yalta

insights.claim: Xi Jinping is the summit's central figure because China is the power with the least need of concessions from the US or Russia.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Treat China as the party with negotiating leverage in US-China-Russia dealings; price outcomes accordingly.
insights.quote: Xi is the leader of the power with the least need of concessions from the others.
insights.locator: If that was his judgement, it is wrong

insights.claim: By attending the Shenzhen summit, Trump gives up the US's strongest post-1945 asset — its role as 'leader of the free world' — and is described as a supplicant for whom negotiating is dangerous.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Erosion of US soft power and alliance credibility raises geopolitical risk premia for US-aligned allies.
insights.quote: President Trump is a supplicant at this meeting – to the point where it is dangerous for him to enter into negotiations.

insights.claim: Putin gains the most from the summit: Russia's economy is dwindling with 40% of production diverted to the Ukraine war and almost half a million military dead reported, yet the summit lets him appear as one of the world's three main leaders.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Summit legitimacy is a reputational win for Moscow that does not fix a war-strained economy; watch for Russia leveraging it diplomatically.
insights.quote: Its economy is dwindling, with 40 per cent of production diverted to his war in Ukraine.
insights.locator: Unlike Trump, Putin has much to gain

insights.claim: China holds a structural trump card over the US via critical minerals: when Trump threatened tariffs after the South Korea deal a year ago, he swiftly backed down once Xi threatened to withhold minerals supplies.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Critical-minerals supply is China's escalation lever; US tariff threats against China are likely to be walked back, capping trade-war tail risk but sustaining supply-chain vulnerability.
insights.quote: he threatened tariffs only to swiftly back down when Xi threatened to withhold minerals supplies, he will find he has a weak hand
insights.locator: Trump may also want to push China on critical minerals

insights.claim: Trump, Jensen Huang and commerce secretary Howard Lutnick have facilitated the Nvidia top-chip trade with China despite opposition from Congress and Trump's top team, and Xi may press for continued supply whether legally exported or via intermediaries.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Nvidia China revenue is tied to Trump's personal stance; any reversal risks Chinese retaliation on minerals.
insights.quote: Trump, Huang and commerce secretary Howard Lutnick have facilitated the chip trade with China

insights.claim: Jensen Huang has been removed as Nvidia CEO over a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, which complicates the US-China chip-export picture.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Leadership change at Nvidia adds governance and policy uncertainty to its China chip sales.
insights.quote: The defenestration of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO over a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy complicates the picture.

insights.claim: If Trump tries to reverse course and curb chip sales to China, Xi would likely threaten to turn off critical minerals supply again.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Chip export tightening and minerals export curbs are linked; hedge both together in semis and EV/defence supply chains.
insights.quote: Should Trump try to change direction, it would not be surprising if Xi threatened to turn off minerals supply once again.
insights.locator: Should Trump try to change direction

insights.claim: Trump wants to discuss curbing the growth or renewal of nuclear arsenals partly to reduce cost, but China has called it a non-starter because its arsenal is far behind those of the US and Russia.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Do not expect arms-control breakthroughs; continued nuclear modernisation spending is the base case.
insights.quote: But China has said from the beginning this is a non-starter
insights.locator: He wants to talk about curbing the growth

insights.claim: Ukraine bombed Russia's Kerch bridge to Crimea ahead of the summit; the main span lies in rubble, blocking maritime traffic and resupply of Russian troops.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Disruption of Kerch Strait shipping and Crimean logistics matters for Black Sea/Azov shipping and Russia's war capacity.
insights.quote: The main span lies in rubble, blocking maritime traffic and the resupply of Russian troops fighting Ukraine.
insights.locator: With this summit in mind, Ukraine this week bombed

insights.claim: China is quietly stirring the Ukraine conflict by buying Russian oil and selling Russia engines and components used in aerial warfare, because a Europe preoccupied with the war suits Beijing.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: China has an incentive to prolong the war; expect continued Chinese purchases of Russian oil and sanctions-evasion flows.
insights.quote: Having Europe preoccupied with the conflict suits China fine.
insights.locator: The wars in Ukraine and Iran

insights.claim: China has no incentive to engage on Iran, described as a war of Trump's making from which he is trying to extricate the US, so neither Ukraine nor Iran is likely to get useful attention at the summit.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: No summit-driven de-escalation in Iran; Middle East energy risk premia unlikely to compress on this event.
insights.quote: China has no incentive to get involved in Iran, a war of Trump’s making from which he is trying to extricate the US.
insights.locator: The wars in Ukraine and Iran

insights.claim: The key risk for Ukraine is that Trump uses the summit to push a peace that gives Russia territory it has not seized by force; Ukraine stressed its Kerch strike was done without Starlink, which it accuses the US of throttling to pressure Kyiv.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Watch for territorial-concession peace proposals and US leverage via Starlink; Ukraine is diversifying away from US-controlled tech.
insights.quote: The danger for Ukraine is that Trump uses this summit to try to advance his notion of peace, including giving Russia territory it has not managed to seize by force.
insights.locator: The danger for Ukraine is that Trump

insights.claim: Ukraine can hold out only with European help, as a Democrat-dominated Congress after the mid-terms, though tougher on Putin, is unlikely to send more funds to Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: The burden of Ukraine financing shifts to Europe — supportive for European defence budgets and EU joint borrowing.
insights.quote: Ukraine will be able to hold out, but only with European help.
insights.locator: Ukraine will be able to hold out

insights.claim: Europe is targeted by all three leaders: Trump disputes its defence dependency and alleged cultural decline, China opposes tariffs the EU is considering on its exports, and Russia probes European unity over Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: European assets carry pressure from three directions; watch EU-China tariff decisions and transatlantic defence friction.
insights.quote: Europe, not present at this summit, is in the crosshairs of all three leaders.
insights.locator: Europe, not present at this summit

insights.claim: Chatham House warns that Chinese technological competition threatens to annihilate European manufacturing, while Europe's main security guarantor, the US, grows unpredictable — creating strong incentives for a common European front on security and trade.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Expect European industrial-protection measures (tariffs on Chinese goods) and higher defence spending; European manufacturers face existential China competition.
insights.quote: technological competition from China threatens to annihilate their manufacturing industries
insights.locator: European leaders, including the UK, need to look hard

insights.claim: Smaller countries will respond to the summit by counting friends and forming new alliances, as the smaller the country the more it depends on international law and institutions such as the UN.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Anticipate realignment and coalition-building among middle and small powers as US leadership recedes.
insights.quote: The smaller the country, the more it needs the rule of international law and respect for international institutions.
insights.locator: Other countries will look at the same photograph
